development.what: the ARC-AGI-1 training split: the vocabulary of capability/grid-dsl.mjs was written against it

heldOut.what: none: this run grades the training split itself

split.contaminated: the training split is the one the vocabulary was written against, so this run is in sample

selection.what: a fixed seed draw of 100 tasks: mulberry32 seed 33, a Fisher Yates shuffle of the sorted ids, the first 100, sorted

heldFixed: the depth (4) and the vocabulary (196 words and learners, capability/grid-dsl.mjs unchanged) are held fixed on this board; only the clock and the attempts move
secondAttemptRule: Two attempts per task, ARC's own rule: a task is right when every test input is answered right by either attempt. The search takes programs that fit every train pair (checked through grid.dsl.match cells) in the order it finds them and stops at two; a program counts as a new attempt only when its test outputs differ from every earlier attempt on at least one test input. So the two attempts are the first two programs found whose test outputs differ, and when only one such answer is found before the clock ends attempt 2 is empty. The two are listed by program length (base words, a learned last step counted as one, a macro as the words it stands for), then by discovery order (capability/grid-search.mjs orderAttempts); solvedFirst stays the program found first, which is the answer a one attempt run gives, so no task a one attempt run solves can be lost by the order.
price: PRICE: 100 tasks at 3000 ms, 2 attempts, 12 workers: 100 priced at the whole 3000 ms clock (at the 3000 ms point they ran to the clock or stopped with fewer than 2 answers), 0 at their wall there (they finished early and will again); 300 task seconds, about 0.42 minutes of wall over 12 workers (plus up to 4000 ms grace on a task killed at the hard deadline); a CPU price: lanes the memory rule holds idle are not in it

PRICE: 100 tasks at 30000 ms, 2 attempts, 12 workers: 100 priced at the whole 30000 ms clock (at the 3000 ms point they ran to the clock or stopped with fewer than 2 answers), 0 at their wall there (they finished early and will again); 3000 task seconds, about 4.17 minutes of wall over 12 workers (plus up to 4000 ms grace on a task killed at the hard deadline); a CPU price: lanes the memory rule holds idle are not in it

memoryRule.what: a lane starts a task only under admitMb of process memory and rampMs (at most a twentieth of the clock) after the last start (or when nothing runs); over preemptMb the task started last is stopped and run again from its start later (at most maxPreempts times); a preempted run writes no row, so every row is one whole run at the whole clock; each worker has a heapMb old generation limit

published.system: Icecuber (Kaggle, program search over a hand written DSL, no LLM)

statement: On the ARC-AGI-1 training split (100 of 400 tasks, a fixed seed draw of 100 tasks: mulberry32 seed 33, a Fisher Yates shuffle of the sorted ids, the first 100, sorted) the grid program search, no model, depth 4 and the same 196 word vocabulary throughout, solved: 37 of 100 (37 percent) at 3000 ms with 1 attempt, then 41 of 100 (41 percent) at 3000 ms with 2 attempts, then 44 of 100 (44 percent) at 30000 ms with 2 attempts. At the longest clock 46 tasks still ran out of clock, 9 found programs that fit every train pair and missed a test output, 1 exhausted the vocabulary. Paired by task id with 3000 ms, 1 attempt, the 3000 ms point with 2 attempts gained 4 and lost 0; Paired by task id with 3000 ms, 2 attempts, the 30000 ms point with 2 attempts gained 4 and lost 1. The clock bought 3 solved tasks per tenfold of clock from 3000 to 30000 ms. This is the TRAINING split, in sample (the vocabulary was written against it), run as the control of the evaluation curve. This file is not the bar: a --limit or --ids run grades part of the split; the training split is in sample (the vocabulary was written against it): the CONTROL of the curve, not the bar. Latencies were measured on a machine shared with other builders.
